overview: September 1st saw a mix of new features and correctness fixes across the BPF subsystem. Highlights include Anton Protopopov's series extending BPF LSM programs to hook into ethtool and generic netlink paths, Anastasios Papagiannis's new kfuncs for safely reading remote process memory via mm_struct, and Hui Zhu's kfunc for BPF-driven proactive memcg memory reclaim. Jiri Olsa introduced a JIT dry-run mode for x86, Fuyu Zhao landed selective BTF module loading in libbpf, and Eric Biggers switched the BPF crypto layer to use the optimized AES-CBC and AES-ECB libraries.

patches.title: bpf: Allow BPF LSM programs to attach to more hooks
patches.author: Anton Protopopov
patches.summary: The first patch in a 7-part series titled 'Add new way to add BPF LSM hooks', this change relaxes the BPF LSM attach restriction so that programs can attach to any tracepoint-style hook exported by kernel subsystems, not just the existing hand-curated list. Subsequent patches in the series add a generic netlink hook on msg_rcv and a new set of ethtool hooks covering the control path, with selftests for both. This significantly extends the reach of BPF-based security policy enforcement into network control-plane operations without requiring a dedicated LSM implementation per subsystem.

patches.title: bpf: Add user memory access kfuncs for mm_struct
patches.author: Anastasios Papagiannis
patches.summary: Part of a 7-patch v3 series ('bpf: Add user memory access kfuncs for mm_struct'), this patch adds kfuncs that allow BPF programs to safely read strings and data from another process's virtual address space given a trusted mm_struct pointer. The series also adds copy_remote_mm_str() to the mm layer, teaches the verifier to track linux_binprm->mm as a trusted-or-null pointer, and relaxes BTF pointer reads for that new annotation. The primary motivation is enabling BPF LSM programs attached to exec hooks to inspect the new process's memory layout before it begins running.

patches.title: mm/bpf: Add bpf_proactive_reclaim kfunc
patches.author: Hui Zhu
patches.summary: The first patch in a 2-part v6 series ('bpf: BPF-driven proactive memcg reclaim'), this adds bpf_proactive_reclaim(), a new kfunc that allows BPF programs to trigger asynchronous memory reclaim against a specific memcg. The design lets a BPF program running in response to memory pressure events drive reclaim policy from userspace-defined logic rather than relying solely on the kernel's built-in heuristics. The companion patch adds a selftest exercising the async reclaim path under real allocation pressure.

patches.title: bpf, x86: Split x86_call_depth_emit_accounting in two functions
patches.author: Jiri Olsa
patches.summary: The opening patch in Jiri Olsa's 3-part series adding a JIT dry-run mode for x86 BPF programs. The series first refactors call-depth accounting into separable emit and non-emit halves, then introduces a JIT emission context struct that abstracts the difference between a real emit pass and a dry run, and finally wires up the dry-run path so the JIT can compute final instruction offsets without allocating executable memory. This is intended to improve JIT reliability and enable future work on exact-size program allocation.

patches.title: libbpf: support selective kernel module BTF loading via bpf_object_open_opts
patches.author: Fuyu Zhao
patches.summary: The first patch in a 2-part v6 series ('libbpf: Improve BPF load performance by selectively loading module BTFs'), this adds a new kern_btf_module_allowlist field to bpf_object_open_opts that lets callers restrict which kernel module BTFs libbpf loads at open time. Programs that only use types from a small set of modules previously incurred the full cost of loading all available module BTFs on the system. The companion patch adds a selftest that verifies only the requested modules are loaded when an allowlist is provided.

patches.title: bpf: crypto: Use AES-CBC and AES-ECB libraries
patches.author: Eric Biggers
patches.summary: This single-patch change switches the BPF crypto helper implementation from the heavyweight crypto API (which uses the full request/scatterlist pipeline) to the new lightweight AES-CBC and AES-ECB library interfaces introduced in the crypto subsystem. The library interfaces are faster for the small, synchronous, non-AEAD encryption that BPF crypto helpers perform, and eliminate the need to allocate and manage crypto_skcipher objects. The change is a pure optimization with no user-visible behavioral difference for existing BPF programs using bpf_crypto_encrypt/decrypt.

patches.title: bpf: Cancel special fields in resizable hashtab on recycle
patches.author: chenyuan
patches.summary: The first patch in a 4-part v3 series fixing correctness issues in the resizable BPF hashtable (rhtab) when map entries containing special fields (kptrs, timers, bpf_rb_node links) are recycled rather than freed. Without the fix, recycled elements could carry stale kptr or timer state into their next use, leading to use-after-free or lost destructor calls. A companion patch fixes a related use-after-free of program BTF in a mem-alloc destructor path, and two selftests cover kptr recycle from NMI context and various special-field combinations.
